What is the advantage of having books as .epub and similar ebook formats instead of having them as PDFs?
So that Amazon can take the books back after you paid. The advantage for Amazon anyway.

You can reflow the text and paging if you change text size. PDFs take up a lot of disk space for the text they represent. PDFs don't preserve sentence or block structure of the text (useful for intelligent line and page breaking if you reflow).

PDF is useful when you want the doc to look exactly the same. Not everyone likes to read at the same text size, or maybe you wanted to read that paper without a two column layout.

Edit: I don't know how well epub or other book formats accomplish this. I still prefer paper or at least open formats (txt, html).

Epubs are fine with reflowing. Most PDFs are a pain on mobile, because, as you correctly said, PDFs are made to look the same everywhere and they're usually not optimized for small screens.

Source: I read epubs on my smartphone.

Edit: I don't know how well epub or other book formats accomplish this

Poorly. .epub is really just zipped html, xml, and images. Much like Web sites, how an epub book looks is highly dependent on the reader. Which gives flexibility but you can't insure that the book will look exactly the same on every reader.
.epub is an open standard (it's really just HTML) but some vendors add DRM that lock it in to a specific software/device
I can adjust text size and formatting, and I know of no PDF reader that lets you look up words, or sync reading position between devices.
